title: Michelin Star Restaurants in India: Is There a Guide Yet?
description: India has no Michelin-starred restaurants yet, as the MICHELIN Guide doesn't cover it. When that may change, and where Indian chefs hold stars abroad.
h1: Are There Michelin Star Restaurants in India?
summary: Why India has no Michelin stars yet, when the guide may arrive, and the Indian restaurants that hold stars abroad.
keywords: how many michelin star restaurants in india
body:
No. There are no Michelin star restaurants in India, because the MICHELIN Guide has never inspected restaurants there. That should change: in September 2026 India’s tourism ministry said a deal to bring the guide to India was in its final stages, with six months of inspections to follow.

So the honest answer to “how many Michelin star restaurants are in India?” is zero, for now. It says nothing about the cooking. Michelin only awards stars in the countries and cities it publishes a guide for, and it has never published one for India. Below we explain why, what the planned deal involves, and where to find Michelin-starred Indian cooking today: 22 restaurants in 6 countries, with their prices.

Why India has no Michelin stars

A Michelin star can only go to a restaurant that Michelin’s inspectors visit, and they only work in places with a guide. Each new guide is a business decision, and in recent years most have launched in partnership with a national or regional tourism body that helps fund the inspections. The newest guides show the pattern: New Zealand’s first selection was revealed in June 2026, and South Australia’s first stars are due on 14 October 2026 under a deal with the state government.

India’s size is part of the challenge. In other large countries Michelin’s first guides started with one or two cities, as in the United States with New York and in mainland China with Shanghai, and an Indian guide would probably begin the same way. Michelin hasn’t said which cities it would cover.

When will India get the MICHELIN Guide?

In September 2026 Suman Billa, Director General of India’s Ministry of Tourism, told the New Indian Express Tourism Summit in Chennai that the ministry was in the final stages of an agreement with Michelin. Reports from the summit say the deal is expected to be signed by the end of 2026, after which Michelin would spend about six months inspecting restaurants across India. On that timetable, the first MICHELIN Guide India selection, and with it the first Indian stars, would come no earlier than the second half of 2027.

Nothing has been signed yet, and Michelin itself hasn’t announced an Indian guide. We’ll update this page, and add a page for every Indian city in the guide with its restaurants’ prices, as soon as the first selection is published.

India already has MICHELIN Keys

Michelin does already rate Indian hotels. Its MICHELIN Key, the hotel equivalent of a star, has covered India since 2025, and the 2026 selection, published in September, gives Keys to 47 Indian hotels, up from 36 the year before. Two hold the top three Keys: Taj Falaknuma Palace in Hyderabad and Taj Lake Palace in Udaipur. A Key rates the whole stay, not the restaurant, so none of these hotels’ restaurants has a Michelin star.

Michelin star Indian chefs and restaurants around the world

Indian cooking has held Michelin stars for a quarter of a century. In 2001 Tamarind and Zaika in London became the first Indian restaurants to win one, under chefs Atul Kochhar and Vineet Bhatia. Today 22 Indian restaurants hold stars: 1 with three, 4 with two and 17 with one. London has the most, with 8, followed by Bangkok and Dubai.

The standout is Trèsind Studio in Dubai, chef Himanshu Saini’s tasting-menu restaurant and the only Indian restaurant in the world with three Michelin stars. In Bangkok, Garima Arora, the first Indian woman to win a Michelin star, holds two at Gaa. In London, the Sethi family’s Gymkhana holds two, and Aktar Islam’s Opheem in Birmingham is the UK’s other two-star Indian restaurant.

The nearest Michelin stars to India

Until India has its own guide, the closest starred dining is a short flight west or east. Dubai and Abu Dhabi have the MICHELIN Guide’s Gulf selections, including Trèsind Studio. Doha has its own guide. To the east, Bangkok has three starred Indian restaurants, and Singapore and Hong Kong are two of Asia’s most-starred cities.

faq.q: How many Michelin star restaurants are there in India?
faq.a: None. The MICHELIN Guide doesn’t cover India, so no Indian restaurant has been inspected or awarded a star. India’s tourism ministry said in September 2026 that a deal to bring the guide to India was in its final stages, with six months of inspections to follow once it is signed.

faq.q: Does India have a MICHELIN Guide?
faq.a: Not for restaurants. Michelin does rate Indian hotels with MICHELIN Keys: 47 hold Keys in the 2026 selection. A restaurant guide with stars is expected only after the government’s agreement with Michelin is signed and the inspections are done.

faq.q: Which Indian restaurant has three Michelin stars?
faq.a: Trèsind Studio in Dubai, led by chef Himanshu Saini, is the only Indian restaurant in the world with three Michelin stars.

faq.q: Who was the first Indian chef to win a Michelin star?
faq.a: Atul Kochhar at Tamarind and Vineet Bhatia at Zaika, both in London, won the first Michelin stars for Indian restaurants in 2001. Garima Arora became the first Indian woman to win a star, at Gaa in Bangkok.

faq.q: Where is the nearest Michelin-starred restaurant to India?
faq.a: The closest guides to India are in the Gulf (Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Doha) and South-East Asia (Bangkok, Singapore and Kuala Lumpur). Dubai and Bangkok both have starred Indian restaurants.
